identity_marker: a glassblower wearing protective sleeves holding a long, hollow, stainless steel blowpipe
continuity_anchors: inside a dimly lit glassblowing studio illuminated by the intense, roaring orange glow of a high-temperature glass furnace
video_goal: Demonstrate the precise technique of gathering a starter bubble of molten glass from a furnace using a steel blowpipe.
single_prompt: A medium shot captures a glassblower wearing protective sleeves holding a long, hollow, stainless steel blowpipe horizontally, resting the tip just inside the furnace opening. The tip of the tool glows a dull red as the glassblower slowly rotates the metal shaft with bare hands. Stepping forward, the glassblower pushes the metal shaft deeper into the bright orange, glowing furnace crucible. The tip of the tool hovers just above the flat, glowing pool of molten glass inside the crucible. The steel tip dips downward, breaking the surface of the bright orange molten glass. Bare hands rapidly twist the shaft, spinning it continuously in a clockwise direction. The glowing orange molten glass spools thickly around the spinning tip, resembling honey wrapping around a dipper. Maintaining the continuous spinning motion, the glassblower slightly raises the angle of the tool, lifting the gathered glass out of the pool. Keeping the shaft rotating, the glassblower slowly pulls the tool backward toward the furnace door. A thin, glowing thread of molten glass stretches from the pool and snaps off as the gather clears the crucible edge. Fully extracting the tool from the furnace, the glassblower reveals a glowing, bulbous gather of glass on the end. Resting the pipe on a metal yoke stand, the glassblower continuously rolls the shaft back and forth to keep the glowing molten glass perfectly centered.
